of [[def-absolutely-continuous-with-respect-to-a-positive-measure]]. If

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

The observed marginal density is
$$
m(\theta,x):=\int_{\mathsf Z}p(\theta,x,z)\,\mu(dz).
$$
The valid-fibre set is
$V:=\{(\theta,x):0<m(\theta,x)<\infty\}$. Only on $V$ define the normalized
latent-fibre density
$$
q(z\mid\theta,x):=\frac{p(\theta,x,z)}{m(\theta,x)}.
$$

No sigma-algebra on $\Theta$ or measurability of $L_x$ is implied. Each density is determined only
$\mu$-almost everywhere; there is no canonical pointwise version and, for
arbitrary uncountable $\Theta$, no common exceptional null set is asserted.

On every valid
fibre $0<m(\theta,x)<\infty$, $q(z\mid\theta,x)=p(\theta,x,z)/m(\theta,x)$ is a measurable
$\mu$-density of total mass one.
\displaystyle\frac{\int_Ap(x,y)\,\mu(dx)}{m(y)}

Assume AC for the supplied existence theorem. Write $E[X\mid\mathcal G]$ for the unique class in $L^1(\Omega,\mathcal G,P|_{\mathcal G})$ consisting of conditional-expectation versions of $X$. A chosen real $\mathcal G$-measurable representative is a **version**.
Assume AC. For every real integrable $X$ on $(\Omega,\mathcal F,P)$ and every sub-sigma-algebra $\mathcal G$, a conditional-expectation version of $X$ given $\mathcal G$ exists.

Assume AC. If $\phi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is finite convex and both $X$ and $\phi(X)$ are integrable, then $\phi(E[X\mid\mathcal G])\le E[\phi(X)\mid\mathcal G]$ almost surely; the left side is measurable and integrable.

If $P\not\ll Q$, define $D(P\|Q)=+\infty$. If $P\ll Q$, assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as in [[def-likelihood-ratio-as-rn-derivative]] and let $r=dP/dQ$ be a finite-valued nonnegative measurable representative of its Radon–Nikodym class; such a representative exists by [[lem-radon-nikodym-density-of-a-finite-positive-measure-has-a-nonnegative-representative]].

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be an arbitrary measure space. Let $f,g:X\to[0,+\infty]$ be measurable. Then
$$\int g\,d(f\,d\mu)=\int gf\,d\mu.$$

Assume AC and use the directional convention of
[[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]]. For probability measures $P,Q$ on one
measurable space, $D(P\|Q)\ge0$, and $D(P\|Q)=0$ if and only if $P=Q$.

Let $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$ be a measurable parameter space, let $(\mathsf X,\mathcal A,\nu)$ and $(\mathsf Z,\mathcal C,\mu)$ be sigma-finite measure spaces, and supply a jointly measurable complete-data density $p(\theta,x,z)$ relative to $\nu\otimes\mu$ that integrates to one on each parameter fiber, as in [[def-latent-variable-joint-and-observed-data-factorization]]. This joint measurability is supplied explicitly and is not inferred from separate likelihood-density versions ([[def-likelihood-density]]). Write
$$
m_\theta(x):=\int_{\mathsf Z}p(\theta,x,z)\,\mu(dz),\qquad q_\theta^x(z):=\frac{p(\theta,x,z)}{m_\theta(x)}
$$
only when $0<m_\theta(x)<\infty$. By [[thm-observed-density-is-latent-marginal-under-tonelli]], $m_\theta$ is the observed-data density and $q_\theta^x$ is a probability density on every such fiber. The observed log likelihood is $\ell_x(\theta):=\log m_\theta(x)$ on those fibers.

Fix observed data $x$. At each valid iterate $\theta_t$, set $q_t:=q_{\theta_t}^x$ and define
$$
Q(\theta\mid\theta_t):=\int_{\mathsf Z}\log p(\theta,x,z)\,q_t(z)\,\mu(dz)
$$
only for candidates where this integral is finite. Choose an initial value $\theta_0$ with $0<m_{\theta_0}(x)<\infty$ and finite $Q(\theta_0\mid\theta_0)$. Use $\log0=-\infty$ and set $q_t|\log p|=0$ wherever $q_t=0$. The Q integral itself is choice-free. To test finite KL when $q_t\mu\ll q_\theta^x\mu$, assume AC as required by [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]]; when absolute continuity fails, $D=+\infty$ by that definition without AC. An **admissible candidate** $\theta$ also satisfies $0<m_\theta(x)<\infty$, $q_t\mu\ll q_\theta^x\mu$, and
$$
D(q_t\mu\|q_\theta^x\mu)<\infty,
$$
where the direction of $D$ is that of [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]]. Require $\int q_t|\log p(\theta,x,\cdot)|\,d\mu<\infty$ for each candidate and $\int q_t|\log p(\theta_t,x,\cdot)|\,d\mu<\infty$ for the current iterate.

The procedure takes a caller-supplied update mode and candidate selector. At each iteration it forms $q_t$ and $Q(\cdot\mid\theta_t)$. In **exact mode**, it selects an attained maximizer of $Q$ over an admissible candidate set containing $\theta_t$. In **generalized mode**, it selects any admissible $\theta_{t+1}$ with $Q(\theta_{t+1}\mid\theta_t)\ge Q(\theta_t\mid\theta_t)$. It stops if a required positive finite marginal, finite $Q$ value, or admissible update is unavailable. The procedure asserts no convergence or global-optimality property and makes no assertion for a candidate that loses current latent support.

derivations.claim: Normalize the current and candidate latent densities on their positive finite fibers; use the assumed directional absolute continuity to ensure the candidate complete-data density is positive under the current latent law.

Transpose the supplied jointly measurable density to Z×X; Tonelli gives a joint probability density and the conditional-density result identifies the current quotient as the latent conditional law at the valid observation fiber.

Construct q_t/q_theta directly as the Radon–Nikodym derivative, then apply the density-integration theorem separately to the positive and negative parts of its logarithm before substituting normalized densities to derive the exact Q/KL identity.

The current latent law is supported where the candidate density is positive. Its exponential complete-data log ratio integrates only over current support, so its expectation is positive and bounded above by the full observed marginal ratio; conditional Jensen therefore gives the Q lower bound without assuming candidate support is contained in current support.
The directional KL term is nonnegative under AC, so the exact identity has a nonnegative gap and confirms the Q lower bound.
A generalized update has nondecreasing Q by definition, and an attained exact maximizer over a set containing the current iterate does too; the Q lower bound yields likelihood ascent in both cases.

The procedure takes a caller-supplied update mode and candidate selector. At each iteration it forms $q_t$ and $Q(\cdot\mid\theta_t)$. In **exact mode**, it selects an attained maximizer of $Q$ over an admissible candidate set containing $\theta_t$. In **generalized mode**, it selects any admissible $\theta_{t+1}$ with $Q(\theta_{t+1}\mid\theta_t)\ge Q(\theta_t\mid\theta_t)$. It stops if a required positive finite marginal, finite $Q$ value, or admissible update is unavailable. The procedure asserts no convergence or global-optimality property and makes no assertion for a candidate that loses current latent support.
Consequently, any admissible update with $Q(\theta\mid\theta_t)\ge Q(\theta_t\mid\theta_t)$ does not decrease $\ell_x$.
The exact M-step also requires an attained Q maximum; ascent itself does not supply one.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Assume AC. For $m\in\mathbb R$ and $\sigma>0$, the normal law $N(m,\sigma^2)$
of [[def-standard-normal-and-normal-laws]] has Lebesgue density
$$g_{m,\sigma}(y)=\frac1\sigma\frac{e^{-((y-m)/\sigma)^2/2}}{\sqrt{2\pi}}=\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^2}}e^{-(y-m)^2/(2\sigma^2)}.$$

The observed marginal density is
$$
m(\theta,x):=\int_{\mathsf Z}p(\theta,x,z)\,\mu(dz).
$$
The valid-fibre set is
$V:=\{(\theta,x):0<m(\theta,x)<\infty\}$. Only on $V$ define the normalized
latent-fibre density
$$
q(z\mid\theta,x):=\frac{p(\theta,x,z)}{m(\theta,x)}.
$$
Consequently, any admissible update with $Q(\theta\mid\theta_t)\ge Q(\theta_t\mid\theta_t)$ does not decrease $\ell_x$.
The exact M-step also requires an attained Q maximum; ascent itself does not supply one.

At zero the collapsing component contributes at least 1/(2 sqrt(2 pi) epsilon), while at one the fixed component contributes at least 1/(2 sqrt(2 pi)); multiplying proves L_epsilon>=1/(8 pi epsilon), which is unbounded as epsilon decreases to zero.
The one-step ascent results neither bound this unbounded likelihood nor produce a parameter attaining its supremum.

If $P\not\ll Q$, define $D(P\|Q)=+\infty$.

This joint measurability is supplied explicitly and is not inferred from separate likelihood-density versions ([[def-likelihood-density]]). Write
$$
m_\theta(x):=\int_{\mathsf Z}p(\theta,x,z)\,\mu(dz),\qquad q_\theta^x(z):=\frac{p(\theta,x,z)}{m_\theta(x)}
$$
only when $0<m_\theta(x)<\infty$. By [[thm-observed-density-is-latent-marginal-under-tonelli]], $m_\theta$ is the observed-data density and $q_\theta^x$ is a probability density on every such fiber. The observed log likelihood is $\ell_x(\theta):=\log m_\theta(x)$ on those fibers.

Fix observed data $x$. At each valid iterate $\theta_t$, set $q_t:=q_{\theta_t}^x$ and define
$$
Q(\theta\mid\theta_t):=\int_{\mathsf Z}\log p(\theta,x,z)\,q_t(z)\,\mu(dz)
$$
only for candidates where this integral is finite. Choose an initial value $\theta_0$ with $0<m_{\theta_0}(x)<\infty$ and finite $Q(\theta_0\mid\theta_0)$. Use $\log0=-\infty$ and set $q_t|\log p|=0$ wherever $q_t=0$. The Q integral itself is choice-free. To test finite KL when $q_t\mu\ll q_\theta^x\mu$, assume AC as required by [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]]; when absolute continuity fails, $D=+\infty$ by that definition without AC. An **admissible candidate** $\theta$ also satisfies $0<m_\theta(x)<\infty$, $q_t\mu\ll q_\theta^x\mu$, and
$$
D(q_t\mu\|q_\theta^x\mu)<\infty,
$$
where the direction of $D$ is that of [[def-kullback-leibler-divergence]]. Require $\int q_t|\log p(\theta,x,\cdot)|\,d\mu<\infty$ for each candidate and $\int q_t|\log p(\theta_t,x,\cdot)|\,d\mu<\infty$ for the current iterate.
